html:
Mugham is the classical music of Azerbaijan, a modal art in which a singer, often with a tar lute and a kamancha fiddle, improvises on set melodies and poems. In the 1800s Shusha in Karabakh was its main school.

It is related to the maqam traditions of Iran, the Arab world and Central Asia. Singers draw on classical Persian and Azerbaijani poetry, such as that of Nizami and Fuzuli. Uzeyir Hajibeyov joined it with Western opera in 1908, and in the 1960s musicians such as Vagif Mustafazadeh blended it with jazz. In 2003 UNESCO proclaimed it a masterpiece of the intangible heritage of humanity. It remains at the heart of Azerbaijani identity.
